Round 350 is planned and `b-next.json` says **CONTINUE**. `store/` was not touched: K2 reads `7f56989 0`.

**Round 349 is closed as PASS.** C passed all 10 rows in the real browser, with 0 bugs. The anonymous `/studio-lab` and purchase-protection checks passed at both screen sizes. Root published it as `7f56989`, which is the baseline for round 350. The task is archived at `tasks/round-349.md`.

**Round 350 makes video clip drags cheaper (PERF-CAND-VIDEO-TRIM-FADE-COST, stage 1).**
- **Cause:** on every drag move of a video clip, the whole video dock re-rendered, because it subscribed to the drag preview in its main body. The dock accounted for 6 of the 19 components per move for a trim and 6 of the 9 for a fade.
- **Fix:** one source file, `ArrangementVideoDock.tsx`, applied as an exact patch (`b-round-349/sketch/dock.patch.txt`). A also adds 6 unit tests (DP66–DP71) and updates doc 232, with 4 mutants that each test must catch.
- **Consults:** tech-lead and performance-optimizer each found the same High bug in my first sketch. On release, the video picture briefly flashed back to its pre-drag state. The sketch is fixed, and I kept the faulty version as a mutant that C must see caught.

Measured on my sketch in a scratch copy:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Components per move (production perf run) | trim 18.683 → 12.817, fade 8.85 → 2.95, video move 15.75 → 9.883 |
| Rest of the perf run | 70/70 asserts pass, 0 new rows, nothing else changed |
| Video picture during a drag (frame, "no video" caption, fade opacity, Undo) | identical to the current code |
| Picture on release | no stray updates, same as the current code |
| Unit tests that cover the dock | 1768/1768 pass (107 files) |
| Video vs playback sync on the current code (C's new reference) | within 0.014 s at both screen sizes |
